newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS-India PM promises new economic measures.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-India PM promises new economic measures.

text.p: Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Monday that new economic policy measures would be announced this week, in a clear message to investors in India to stop worrying about the government's commitment to reform.
"Some decisions will be coming in the next two to three days," Deve Gowda told the All India Association of Industries.
Parliament's approval will be needed for further measures the government planned to announce in the budget set for February 28, he said.
Stock market investors anticipated good news was on the way, sending the Bombay Stock Exchange benchmark 30-share index 3.7 percent higher during the day with a gain of 127.12 points to 3,562.74.

Share prices have risen around 15 percent since the beginning of the year, having plunged to a three-year low on December 4 as investors lost faith in the ability of Deve Gowda's multi-party coalition to follow through on promises of reform.
Despite the recent surge in share values the markets have remained subject to wild swings, prompting worries that the bullish speculation was overheated.
"My decisions will always be to give more opportunity and create a better investment climate for the investors," Deve Gowda said.
"With this background, forget the question of hesitation in the mind of the government while making decisions," he said.
He said his seven-month old goverment would stick by the policy of economic liberalisation mapped out by the former Congress Party government's finance minister Manmohan Singh.
"We will not deviate from the policies laid down by Manmohan Singh, the previous government. There is no need for a change in the policies. We have accepted them," he said.
Deve Gowda said speculators were to blame for the markets' volatility rather than the government's decision-making abilities.

"The decline in the capital markets or the fluctuation in the capital markets --is it due to policy decisions of the government or due to players in the capital market. I would like the industrialists to tell me," Deve Gowda said.
"In seven months I cannot bring heaven to Earth. In a situation like this the government has to play its role and take a decision," Deve Gowda said.
Deve Gowda said policy decisions would be guided by the need to hit an annual investment target of $10 billion from domestic and foreign investors.
He also said said that government would approve all oustanding power projects within two months.
The prime minister told the conference that new steps would be taken before he and Finance Minister P. Chidambaram went to Switzerland to attend the World Economic Forum in Davos on January 31.
Chidamabaram, speaking on Business Agenda programme broadcast by Star Plus television, said: "We are determined to go through and push reforms. What we need is not less, but more reforms."
"The need is for more restructuring, more liberalisation, more freedom. All this can be done if we take hard decisions and if we take them quickly."

The finance minister said one of those hard decisions was whether to raise state-controlled petroleum product prices in order to alleviate some of the resulting pressures on domestic oil companies, but he gave no hint that a quick decision was in the pipeline.

"It is a difficult question. Do not underestimate the difficulty of raising petroleum prices twice in a year. We took one difficult decision last July (by raising prices) and to ask us to take another within six months is doubly difficult," Chidambaram said.
